papers.title: Inference-Time Consensus for Mitigating Hidden Behaviors from LLM Fine-Tuning

summary.tldr: This paper introduces inference-time consensus decoding to mitigate targeted misbehavior and hidden preferences in LLMs fine-tuned on poisoned or ostensibly benign data by aggregating next-token distributions from multiple reference models.
key_points: The method fine-tunes a separate reference model on each data source and aggregates their next-token distributions at decoding time.

Two consensus decoders are introduced: a token-wise minimum, which caps each token at the lowest probability any source assigns, and a base-relative variant, which reverts to the base probability if sources move in opposing directions.
The approach tolerates partial support across sources and different surface expressions of the same intention, relaxing exact agreement.

Consensus decoding suppresses source-specific misbehavior while preserving shared desirable behavior, outperforming union training and weight averaging in controlled poisoning, subliminal learning, and emergent misalignment tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: This technique offers a robust defense against hidden behaviors and misalignments introduced during LLM fine-tuning, improving model trustworthiness and safety.

papers.title: Confidently Wrong: Exception Chain Collapse in Frontier LLM Rule Evaluation

summary.tldr: Frontier LLMs exhibit "exception chain collapse" in nested rule evaluation, with unstable accuracy that shifts without notice, addressed by a neuro-symbolic architecture for deterministic execution.
key_points: Frontier LLMs fail on nested conditional rules (e.g., "A unless B unless C"), termed exception chain collapse, with observed accuracy drift (e.g., GPT-5.4 on construction insurance improved from 96.6% to 100% silently).
The Aethis Eligibility Module is a neuro-symbolic architecture where LLMs author rules and an SMT-based layer executes them deterministically.
Aethis achieved 20/20 on a 20-scenario adversarial construction insurance benchmark, outperforming three of four frontier configurations.
Aethis demonstrated significantly higher accuracy on 9 LegalBench tasks (949 cases) compared to three frontier models (McNemar's p <= 0.003), with up to +41 points on multi-prong tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: Unstable and unannounced accuracy shifts in frontier LLMs pose significant compliance risks for regulated workflows relying on their evaluation capabilities.

papers.title: When Activation Oracles Learn Not to Read: Concept-Specific Blind Spots in Fine-Tuned Oracles

summary.tldr: Fine-tuned Activation Oracles (AOs) can develop concept-specific blind spots, failing to report hidden information persistently present during their own training, even when the concept is decodable within the oracle.
key_points: Activation Oracles (AOs) are language models trained to answer natural-language questions about another model's internal activations.
In a Taboo Word Guessing setting, fine-tuned AOs became "concept-specific anti-readers," failing to recover a hidden concept despite its persistent presence during training.
This failure is not due to the concept's absence from subject or oracle representations; the target remains decodable inside the oracle.
LogitLens and layer-ablation analyses indicate the failure originates in the AO readout pathway, not in the concept's internal representation.
The study demonstrates that behavioral leakage, representation-level decodability, and AO-verbalizability can diverge.
summary.why_it_matters: This raises reliability concerns for learned interpretability interfaces, as AOs may not accurately report internal model states even when the information is present.

papers.title: What CLIP Knows but Cannot Say: Recovering Negation from Frozen Intermediate Features

summary.tldr: PeakPatch recovers negation sensitivity in CLIP by re-injecting lost syntax from intermediate layers, achieving significant performance gains on negation benchmarks with minimal added parameters.
key_points: CLIP's insensitivity to negation is attributed to Representational Collapse, where compositional syntax in middle layers is lost in final layers as visual alignment increases.
PeakPatch, a post-hoc correction system, intercepts the CLIP text encoder at its 'compositional peak' to recover negation signals without altering pretrained weights.

An Embedding Correction Network (ECN) extracts a negation-specific signal and predicts a deviation vector to re-inject lost syntax into the final embedding space, while a Score Correction Network (SCN) predicts bounded scalar score offsets.
PeakPatch adds 5.2M parameters (3.5% of backbone) and achieves 74.3% on COCO MCQ (+35.1 over CLIP) and 65.5% on VOC MCQ, outperforming fine-tuning baselines on out-of-distribution negation retrieval.
The corrected embeddings improve text-to-image generation (+18.4 negation score) and generalize across ViT-B/32, ViT-L/14, and SigLIP backbones.
summary.why_it_matters: This method significantly enhances the understanding of negation in vision-language models, improving their utility in discriminative tasks and text-to-image generation without extensive retraining.

papers.title: Through the Bottleneck: How Multi-head Latent Attention Separates Content from Position in Language Models

summary.tldr: Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) in DeepSeek-V2 achieves 81% KV-cache reduction by separating content from position, reshaping transformer internal circuits, and over-provisioning its bottleneck capacity.
key_points: The cKV bottleneck learns a pure content representation, retaining 98% entity identity while discarding positional information, validating MLA's separation of content from position via RoPE.
Induction heads co-locate at a single layer (Layer 12) in MLA, unlike their distributed formation in standard Multi-Head Attention (MHA).
A single "semantic hub" layer (Layer 15) exhibits the highest SVD effective rank and strongest disruption-attribution score.
The bottleneck is globally over-provisioned, utilizing only 46% of its capacity on average.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding MLA's internal mechanisms provides insights into how models organize content and position, potentially leading to more efficient and interpretable large language models.

papers.title: Reason Popper-ly: Patching In-Context Reasoning with Inductive Logic Programming

summary.tldr: Reason Popper-ly is a neurosymbolic framework that uses inductive logic programming to learn relation composition rules from LLM reasoning traces and applies them as an online verifier for step-level correction.
key_points: The framework learns relation composition rules from LLM-generated reasoning traces using inductive logic programming (ILP).
It acts as an online verifier, checking each inferred step against learned rules, diagnosing violations, and rewriting incorrect steps with symbolically derived repairs.
After correction, the remaining suffix of the reasoning trace is regenerated, conditioning the LLM on the verified trace.
Evaluated on CLUTRR, Reason Popper-ly improved terminal accuracy by up to 48 percentage points for small models and 15 points for frontier models on 10-hop reasoning chains.
The method provides a fine-grained error taxonomy through step-level ILP verification, offering diagnostic insights beyond final-answer accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: This method improves the reliability and interpretability of LLM multi-step reasoning by ensuring logical soundness at each step, especially for complex tasks.

papers.title: Similarity Is Not Logic: Factored Inference for Dual-Encoder Vision-Language Models

summary.tldr: A new method, factored inference, addresses compositional failures in dual-encoder vision-language models by separating evidence extraction from constraint execution, improving accuracy on logical queries.
key_points: Dual-encoder VLMs exhibit a Bag-of-Concepts effect, where similarity scores approximate mean pooling of concept evidence, leading to failures in compositional queries like "umbrella and no person".
Factored inference separates evidence extraction from constraint execution to resolve compositional failures.
LCSE (Logic-Constrained Score Editing) is a training-free method that executes constraints externally using concept scores from frozen encoders.
LCSE achieves 85.5% accuracy on FACTOR-Bench, outperforming the best fine-tuned baseline (73.2%), and 90.7% when applied to SigLIP 2.
LCSE improves NegBench COCO MCQ accuracy from 27.2% to 65.2% while maintaining retrieval performance.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables more accurate and reliable interpretation of complex, logical queries in zero-shot vision-language tasks without fine-tuning.

papers.title: The Entropic Bound for Transformers: Why Static Rank Fails and Attention-Native Rank Recovers

summary.tldr: This paper introduces an attention-native intrinsic rank for Transformers, extending the Entropic Bound to accurately measure task-intrinsic capacity in both linear and softmax attention models.
key_points: The intrinsic rank r* of the token-mixing operator is a tight lower bound for task-intrinsic capacity in a linear attention surrogate, with gradient descent recovering this rank under low-rank implicit-bias assumptions.
A naive transfer of the static rank concept fails for real attention due to the input-conditioned nature of attention's mixing operator, not softmax or rank constraints.
An attention-native intrinsic rank, defined as the minimum query-key kernel rank, restores the Entropic Bound structure (deficiency, achievability, recovery) for both linear and softmax attention.
The energy effective rank serves as a robust estimator for the attention-native intrinsic rank, even with softmax distortion.
The intrinsic rank is exactly recoverable from data for linear QK attention, but only partially recoverable for softmax attention due to nonlinear inversion and kernel-value identifiability effects.
summary.why_it_matters: This work provides a method to determine the minimum model capacity required for a given task, enabling more efficient Transformer design and training.

papers.title: ConsistencyGate: Preventing Memory Contamination in LLM Agents via Self-Consistency Admission Control

summary.tldr: ConsistencyGate prevents memory contamination in LLM agents by using a self-consistency admission control mechanism to validate facts before committing them to memory.
key_points: ConsistencyGate queries the LLM K times for a soft support score for a candidate fact m extracted from context c, admitting m only if the average score exceeds a threshold.
The mechanism is model-agnostic, requires no fine-tuning, and can operate with a single forward pass using a log-probability variant for low-latency scenarios.
Two real-conversation benchmarks (LoCoMo-Contam, MSC-Contam) and one synthetic corpus (MemContam) were created to evaluate the method.
ConsistencyGate reduced memory contamination across four LLM backbones compared to a write-everything baseline, with costs concentrated on implicitly stated facts.
All three benchmarks and the gate implementation are publicly released.
summary.why_it_matters: This method improves the reliability of LLM agents by ensuring the integrity of their external memory, preventing hallucinated facts from propagating as false premises.

papers.title: Mask2Shield: Strengthening LLM Safety against Neuron-Pruning Attacks

summary.tldr: Mask2Shield (M2S) is a masked-forward alignment method that trains LLMs under functional neuron pruning to strengthen safety against neuron-pruning attacks, reducing successful attacks while preserving capabilities.
key_points: Mask2Shield (M2S) trains a student model under masked-forward alignment, forcing it to recover safe refusal using remaining computation after functional pruning.
A frozen, unmasked teacher model provides complete benign answers during M2S training to limit capability drift in the student.
M2S reduced successful recomputed pruning attacks from 80-279 to 1-44 out of 313 prompts across ten model configurations.
M2S generally preserved four capability benchmarks while mitigating neuron-pruning attacks.
M2S was also evaluated with TwinBreak, a different neuron-selection and iterative pruning method, showing consistent effectiveness.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enhances LLM safety by making targeted neuron-pruning attacks less effective, thereby improving the robustness of safety alignments in deployed models.

papers.title: Directional Influence Function: Estimating Training Data Influence in Constrained Learning

summary.tldr: The Directional Influence Function (DIF) is a novel estimator for training data influence in constrained learning, explicitly incorporating feasibility requirements by formulating optimality conditions as a variational inequality.
key_points: Classical influence functions (IF) are unreliable in constrained settings because data perturbations can alter both the objective and the feasible region, leading to infeasible estimates.
DIF formulates the optimality conditions of constrained learning as a variational inequality (VI) to analyze how training data perturbations affect the VI.
DIF was validated on constrained linear regression, demonstrating accurate recovery of leave-one-out retraining results, unlike IF and penalty-based IF which showed significant bias.
DIF was applied to fairness-constrained CNNs, where it accurately predicted test loss changes under data removal and aligned closely with actual retraining outcomes.
summary.why_it_matters: DIF provides an efficient and reliable method for data attribution in constrained learning, crucial for interpretability and robustness in models with explicit feasibility requirements.

papers.title: Training with (Swap) Regret Loss in a Single-Layer Self-Attention Model: A Case Study on the Probability Simplex

summary.tldr: This paper introduces swap-regret loss and demonstrates that a single-layer self-attention model trained with regret loss can implement no-regret online learning dynamics, leading to game-theoretic equilibrium behaviors.
key_points: A single-layer self-attention model trained with regret loss achieves a stationary point matching smoothed fictitious play, ensuring no-regret behavior.
A new swap-regret loss function extends the regret-loss framework to optimize for swap-deviation robustness.

Swap-regret loss yields a stationary point whose forward pass implements the Blum-Mansour swap-regret update, with each attention head performing an external-regret update via smoothed fictitious play.
Regret-trained attention architectures can realize differentiable mechanisms that induce coarse correlated equilibrium (external-regret) and correlated equilibrium (swap-regret) in games.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables minimal attention architectures to learn online-learning dynamics with game-theoretic guarantees without requiring supervised training data of those algorithms.

papers.title: RareLens: Towards End-to-End Rare Disease Care via Aligning Divergent Large Language Model Reasoning

summary.tldr: RareLens is an AI system that aligns divergent reasoning from heterogeneous large language models to support end-to-end rare disease care, outperforming frontier models.
key_points: RareLens supports primary-visit risk screening, diagnosis, treatment planning, and prognosis through four coordinated modules.
The system exploits variability between heterogeneous large language models, aligning and calibrating their divergent reasoning into actionable decisions.
Evaluated on RareBench (157,525 cases, 33 Orphanet categories, >7,000 conditions), RareLens achieved 0.917 AUC for screening and top-1 accuracies of 65.5% for diagnosis and 89.8% for treatment.
RareLens outperformed GPT-5, DeepSeek-R1, Claude-3.7-Sonnet, and Gemini-2.5-Pro at each stage.
In an external study (1,287 cases, 23 physicians), autonomous RareLens and RareLens-assisted physicians substantially outperformed unaided physicians.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach offers a generalizable strategy for high-uncertainty clinical decision-making by aligning divergent model reasoning rather than scaling a single model.

papers.title: TopoFE: topology-aware LLM-guided Automated Feature Engineering

summary.tldr: TopoFE introduces a topology-aware multi-island evolutionary framework for LLM-guided automated feature engineering, addressing limitations of stateless generation and homogeneous search in existing methods.
key_points: TopoFE employs a multi-island evolutionary framework for LLM-guided feature engineering.
The method integrates family-specialized exploration, adaptive prompt memory, and topology-guided knowledge transfer.
It aims to discover diverse and compositional feature programs, improving upon stateless generation and homogeneous search.
Experiments on 29 public tabular datasets show consistent improvements over state-of-the-art AutoFE methods for classification and regression.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enhances automated feature engineering by generating more diverse and transferable feature programs, leading to improved predictive performance across various tasks and models.

papers.title: Beyond a Global Norm: Personalizing Toxicity Sensitivity in Language Models Without Retraining

summary.tldr: This paper evaluates training-free methods for personalizing language model toxicity sensitivity across pre-decoding, in-decoding, and post-decoding stages, reducing alignment error by 28-47%.
key_points: The study compares training-free methods for aligning language generation to user-specific toxicity sensitivities.
Three inference-time intervention stages were evaluated: pre-decoding (prompt conditioning, rewriting), in-decoding (token, logit, representation steering), and post-decoding (candidate re-ranking).
All evaluated methods reduced alignment error by 28-47% against toxicity sensitivity targets from the PRISM dataset.
A trade-off exists between alignment effectiveness, personalization, and general language quality, indicating toxicity sensitivity alignment is a multi-objective problem.
summary.why_it_matters: Personalizing toxicity sensitivity in language models without retraining allows for more nuanced and user-specific control over generated content.

papers.title: In-Context Learning as Implicit Policy Gradient

summary.tldr: This paper demonstrates that score-conditioned In-Context Learning (ICL) in LLMs structurally corresponds to policy gradient optimization, specifically REINFORCE, and quantifies this relationship empirically.
key_points: Score-conditioned ICL has a structural correspondence to policy gradient optimization.
Self-attention mechanisms can implement reward-weighted aggregation, analogous to REINFORCE, under specific weight matrix configurations.
The correspondence is directional in hidden-state space and holds exactly under simplifying conditions, with empirical quantification of its strength.
An exact upper bound on distribution shift from bounded attention updates is derived, analogous to KL-constrained policy optimization.
LLMs utilize score information to shift output distributions towards high-scoring examples, and attention weights correlate with example scores.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding the theoretical underpinnings of ICL as policy gradient can lead to more principled and effective methods for improving LLM performance through iterative self-correction.

papers.title: SQBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Task Delivery by Language-Model Agents in Production-Oriented Workflows

summary.tldr: SQBench is a new benchmark for evaluating language-model agents on production-oriented task delivery, focusing on verifiable deliverables within constrained workflows, using a 10D Risk Matrix for evaluation beyond functional completion.
key_points: SQBench v1.0 contains 220 standardized tasks organized into L1 atomic capabilities, L2 composite skills, and L3 business scenarios.
Evaluation involves computing functional Completion, then deriving Risk Penalty and Performance from independently evidenced triggers in a 10D Risk Matrix.
A Strict Pass requires Completion = 1 and Risk Penalty = 0; the highest prespecified Weighted Pass@1 is 60.5%.
Mean Strict Pass@1 on L3 is 18.5%, indicating delivery under domain constraints is a shared weakness across configurations.
Of 2,348 results with Completion = 1, 113 (4.8%) failed Strict Pass due to risks like unverifiable citations or format violations.
summary.why_it_matters: This benchmark provides a method to assess the quality of language-model agent outputs in production environments, highlighting risks beyond mere functional completion.

papers.title: Compiler-Grounded Hierarchical Diagnosis for LLM-Based Triton Kernel Optimization

summary.tldr: A new compiler-grounded hierarchical diagnosis system optimizes Triton kernels for NPUs by linking runtime symptoms to IR structure and compiler behavior, achieving significant speedups.
key_points: The system formulates kernel optimization as a progressive cross-layer diagnosis problem, linking runtime symptoms to IR structure and compiler behavior.
It escalates diagnosis from pattern triage and profiling to IR attribution and compiler-grounded analysis, proposing evidence-backed source-level rewrites.
Implemented on Triton for Ascend NPUs, the system was evaluated on 37 NPUKernelBench-derived Ascend 950 benchmarks.
The system achieved a geometric-mean speedup of 4.35x and a median speedup of 2.73x from initial to optimized Triton kernels, with 22/37 exceeding 2x and 13/37 exceeding 5x.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables more effective optimization of LLM-generated kernels on emerging accelerators by diagnosing underlying compiler issues rather than just surface-level performance.

papers.title: Poster: Rethinking Security in LLM Code Generation through Real-World Risk Scenarios

summary.tldr: A new benchmark evaluates LLM code generation security using 2,700 test cases across three real-world risk scenarios, revealing over 56% vulnerability rates and up to 45% improvement with security-aware prompting.
key_points: Identified three real-world risk scenarios for LLM-generated code vulnerabilities: Ambiguous Requirements, Under-Specified Operational Context, and Security--Functionality Conflict.
Constructed a large-scale benchmark of 2,700 test cases for fine-grained evaluation of LLM security.
Evaluated eight state-of-the-art LLMs, finding average vulnerability rates exceeding 56% across risk scenarios.
Demonstrated that security-aware prompting can mitigate risks, achieving up to 45% improvement.
summary.why_it_matters: This research highlights significant security vulnerabilities in LLM-generated code under realistic conditions and demonstrates the effectiveness of security-aware prompting for mitigation.

papers.title: Attention-Guided Layer Selection for Contrastive Decoding in Large Language Models

summary.tldr: This work introduces attention-guided strategies (Attention-JSD, Attention-Entropy-Max, Attention-Entropy-Min) for layer selection in contrastive decoding, outperforming DoLa by leveraging self-attention mechanisms for improved factual accuracy in LLMs.
key_points: DoLa's dynamic layer selection relies on divergences in output vocabulary distributions.
The proposed attention-guided strategies utilize structural information from internal self-attention mechanisms for layer selection.
Attention-JSD and Attention-Entropy-Min strategies consistently outperform the original DoLa on TruthfulQA.
Significant gains were observed on multi-answer metrics (MC2 and MC3) using the new strategies.
summary.why_it_matters: Leveraging attention distributions provides a more sensitive signal for resolving factual knowledge, leading to more accurate LLM outputs.

papers.title: SymStep: Symbolic Step Verification for Logical Reasoning

summary.tldr: SymStep introduces a symbolic step verification method for LLMs in logical reasoning, where an LLM makes atomic claims checked by a constraint propagator, significantly improving performance on constraint-dense tasks.
key_points: SymStep employs an LLM to make one atomic claim at a time (e.g., "DEDUCE: Alice, pet, Cat"), which is then checked for consistency by a lightweight constraint propagator.
The constraint propagator rejects contradictions and automatically cascades implied facts, preventing error accumulation seen in Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting.
SymStep+G incorporates Most-Restricted-Variable (MRV) guidance after each accepted step, directing the LLM towards the most constrained unresolved variable.
SymStep+G achieved 97% on a 35-puzzle subset of ZebraLogicBench, 100% on AR-LSAT, and 100% on LGP-14, outperforming Direct, CoT (0-87%), and Logic-LM (0%).
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables LLMs to reliably solve complex, constraint-dense logical reasoning problems where prior methods fail.

papers.title: MixQuant: Adaptive Mixed-Precision Quantization for Large Language Models

summary.tldr: MixQuant introduces an adaptive mixed-precision quantization framework that considers upstream layer dependencies for improved bit allocation across varying memory budgets.
key_points: MixQuant addresses the limitation of existing adaptive quantization methods that do not account for a layer's sensitivity dependence on upstream layer quantization levels.
It marginalizes each layer's distortion over random quantized upstream configurations to generate budget-agnostic scores.
The framework calibrates quantizer parameters using allocation plans produced by its own allocator and penalizes allocations that assign the lowest bitwidths to layers.
A single greedy pass during deployment serves any memory budget, achieving performance comparable to an ILP solver with negligible overhead.
MixQuant improves average accuracy by up to 8 points and reduces perplexity from 12.43 to 10.70 on Llama-3.2-3B, Llama-2-7B, and Mistral-7B using AWQ and GPTQ.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables more efficient and accurate deployment of large language models across diverse hardware constraints without requiring recalibration for each memory budget.

papers.title: All in One: Generative Modeling as Mean-Field Game Design

summary.tldr: MFGLab unifies twelve generative models as mean-field game special cases, introducing DI-Flow for mode coverage and applying MFG solvers to generative modeling.
key_points: MFGLab is an open-source PyTorch library that unifies twelve generative models (e.g., Continuous Normalizing Flows, OT-Flow, Score-based Models, Schrödinger Bridges) as special cases of a single mean-field game variational problem.
The unification is achieved through a cost tuple API, where all twelve models are specified by four composable cost functions, sharing training loop, log-Jacobian, and reverse-ODE sampler.
DI-Flow is a novel cost design within MFGLab that utilizes a differentiable entropy functional to improve mode coverage.
MFGLab applies learning-based mean-field game (MFG) solvers to generative modeling, demonstrating substantial performance improvements over neural training on stochastic-dynamics rows.
Experiments on 2-D benchmarks confirm that the unified API in MFGLab maintains performance comparable to hand-coded implementations.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework simplifies the development and comparison of diverse generative models by providing a unified mathematical and computational foundation.

papers.title: VecTree-RAG: An Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework Combining Vector and Tree Retrieval for Efficiency and Accuracy

summary.tldr: VecTree-RAG is an agentic RAG framework combining vector search for document ranking and tree traversal for evidence localization, achieving higher accuracy and evidence precision in scientific QA.
key_points: VecTree-RAG uses vector search on compact document/section representations for corpus-level ranking and reasoning-guided traversal of source-verified section trees for evidence localization within shortlisted papers.
It achieved 0.800 LLM-judge correctness on QASPER, 0.925 accuracy on LitQA2, and a 0.547 composite score on MOSAIC, outperforming Dense RAG, reranked Dense RAG, RAPTOR, and Search-o1.
On QASPER, VecTree-RAG demonstrated an evidence-page precision of 0.274, compared to 0.046–0.071 for baselines.
Ablation studies on LitQA2 showed the complete vector-tree architecture required fewer inference tokens than variants lacking tree navigation or corpus-level vector routing.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach offers a structure-aware and traceable architecture for scientific literature question answering, improving efficiency and accuracy by separating document identification from evidence localization.

papers.title: Adversarial Test-Hardening for AI-Written Code: An Instrument Autopsy and a Pre-Registered Causal Estimate of the Critic Loop

summary.tldr: This paper introduces an adversarial test-hardening loop for AI-written code, demonstrating its effectiveness in killing mutants and revealing instrument artifacts in cross-lineage comparisons.
key_points: An adversarial test-hardening loop, using Tester and Critic models with mechanical oracles, killed 105 mutants missed by one-shot generation across five Python subjects in Experiment 1.
An earlier reported cross-lineage effect (p = 9.5e-66) was identified as an instrument artifact due to an output cap silently truncating the verbose model.
In Experiment 2, a pre-registered design showed same-lineage Critic rounds killed 78% of surviving mutants (mean incremental kill rate 0.783, 95% CI [0.592, 0.935]).
Cross-provider configurations showed a positive pilot difference (rate gap 0.178, 95% CI [0.039, 0.347]) at 5.5x lower arm cost, with asymmetries from the harness influencing results.
summary.why_it_matters: This research provides a method to improve the quality of AI-generated code by systematically hardening tests and highlights the critical need for rigorous adversarial review in AI system evaluation.

papers.title: X-Stage: An Overlooked Pipeline Stage for Communication-Computation Overlap in DiT Inference

summary.tldr: Researchers identified X-Stage, a post-issue GPU pipeline stage, and built a Burst-Gap model to predict communication backpressure, enabling kernel optimizations that achieve up to 1.62x speedups in DiT inference.
key_points: X-Stage exposes post-issue communication progress, showing that sustained remote-store bursts exhaust GPU capacity and introduce sender backpressure.
A lightweight Burst-Gap model parameterizes backpressure-free issue time, effective drain rate, and outstanding capacity to predict communication overhead and recovery.
Interleaving Linear-1 and Linear-2 operations in DeepGEMM MegaMoE spaced out remote stores, achieving a 1.18x geomean and 1.62x max speedup over Expert-Wave baselines across 84 configs.
Fusing post-attention All-to-All remote stores with FlashAttention (v3 and v4) at tile granularity enabled max sender-visible speedups of 1.43x and 1.42x without dedicated communication warps.
summary.why_it_matters: Accounting for post-issue communication progress allows GPU kernel developers to eliminate sender backpressure and effectively hide communication overhead in distributed diffusion transformer inference.

papers.title: SeekJudge: A Practical Reward Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Computer-Use Agents

summary.tldr: SeekJudge introduces a multi-agent framework powered by a single distilled 9B model that matches or surpasses rule-based reward supervision in reinforcement learning for computer-use agents.
key_points: Utilizes four role-specialized agents (Condense, Ground, Seek, Analyze) operating in a Seek-Analyze loop over execution trajectories.
Employs a seed-calibrated distillation pipeline to train a single specialized 9B parameter backbone for all four constituent agents.
Provides step-level trajectory judgments with a small per-call context that scales to long-horizon GUI tasks.
Includes architectural reward server optimizations to accelerate inference during online RL training.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes model-based reward modeling as a practical, scalable replacement for fragile rule-based and costly closed-source LLM evaluations in computer-use agent RL.

papers.title: CachedSearch: Training-Free Cached Exploration for Test-Time Search in Video Diffusion

summary.tldr: CachedSearch introduces a training-free test-time search strategy for video diffusion models that uses aggressive caching during candidate exploration and re-denoises only the winning trajectory at full compute.
key_points: Lossy caching preserves candidate ranking, achieving a 0.905 median Spearman rank correlation and 72% top-1 agreement with full-compute rollouts using ImageReward on Wan2.1-14B.
At N=8 search width, CachedSearch retains 94.7% of best-of-N performance gains while reducing compute costs to 63%.
Combining CachedSearch with mid-trajectory pruning increases exploration savings to 3.11x while maintaining an 88.6% gain capture rate.
The method generalizes without retraining across six models and four architectures (Wan, LTX, CogVideoX, and Hunyuan) ranging from 1.3B to 14B parameters.
summary.why_it_matters: It acts as a training-free, verifier-agnostic efficiency layer that doubles the viable search width of video diffusion test-time scaling under fixed compute budgets.

papers.title: False Prophets: On the Security of World Models in Agentic Systems

summary.tldr: Researchers identify critical vulnerabilities in text-based world models used by agentic systems, demonstrating that attackers can induce mispredictions with up to a 95% success rate to trigger malicious actions.
key_points: Identifies world-model-specific security vulnerabilities in terminal-based autonomous agents.
Demonstrates that induced mispredictions lead to unauthorized command execution, denial of service, private data extraction, and wallet drainage.
Achieves up to a 95% success rate in exploiting agentic pipelines by manipulating environment simulators.
Introduces a dedicated security benchmark dataset designed to evaluate text-based world models.
summary.why_it_matters: Relying on approximate world models for action prediction introduces severe security and privacy risks that can compromise the host system during agentic task execution.

papers.title: AgentOmnia: Scaling Agentic Models for Full-Scenario Applications

summary.tldr: AgentOmnia is a framework for full-scenario agentic scaling across ToC, ToB, and ToE domains, integrating an extensible taxonomy, bidirectional data synthesis, post-training algorithms, and PRD-guided self-evolution.
key_points: Constructed 5,018 stateful environments containing 255,375 tools and 52,361 tasks using bidirectional synthesis, tool-dependency, program-structured, and solver-based pipelines.
Employs supervised fine-tuning, online agentic reinforcement learning, and a rollback curriculum to train models, backed by programs, solvers, and verifiers for correctness signals.
Translates evaluation failures from OmniaBench into Product Requirement Documents (PRDs) to enable targeted, self-evolutionary model improvement.
Fine-tuning Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 raised its macro-average score across OmniaBench, τ²-Bench, DeepPlanning, and VitaBench from 22.86% to 41.69%, outperforming Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a unified methodology to systematically scale and evaluate LLM agents across diverse, complex, and stateful real-world application environments.

papers.title: On the Impossibility of Unbiased and Length-Invariant Policy Optimization with Outcome Rewards

summary.tldr: An impossibility theorem proves no length-based weighting in outcome-reward GRPO can simultaneously achieve gradient unbiasedness and length invariance, framing GRPO and Dr. GRPO as extreme ends of a single tradeoff spectrum.
key_points: An impossibility theorem shows no weighting scheme under standard outcome-reward GRPO can simultaneously satisfy gradient unbiasedness (P1) and length invariance (P2).
GRPO satisfies P2 but violates P1, while Dr. GRPO satisfies P1 but violates P2.
The tradeoff is parameterized by f_alpha(L) = L^{alpha - 1}, where alpha = 0 represents GRPO and alpha = 1 represents Dr. GRPO.
In Dr. GRPO, the length bias allows longer trajectories to dominate gradient updates by a factor proportional to the length ratio.
summary.why_it_matters: Practitioners must choose between gradient bias and length bias when scaling reinforcement learning for reasoning models, as neither GRPO nor Dr. GRPO completely resolves length-related gradient distortions.

papers.title: Context-Adaptive Inference: A Unified Statistical and Foundation-Model View

summary.tldr: This paper presents a unified statistical framework for context-adaptive inference, proving that explicit parameter adaptation and implicit expert routing are mathematically equivalent to kernel ridge regression under specific linear conditions.
key_points: Formalizes context-adaptive inference under a unified objective mapping context $c$ to parameters $\theta(c)$ to yield predictions $f(x; \theta(c))$.
Bridges three separate traditions: explicit statistical adaptation, meta-learning/transfer adaptation, and implicit foundation model adaptation (prompting, retrieval, routing).

Proves mathematical equivalence between explicit parameter adaptation, implicit routing, and kernel ridge regression on joint input-context features under squared loss and linear heads with fixed features.
Proposes design principles and metrics to evaluate adaptation-efficiency, routing stability, and context-specific robustness.
summary.why_it_matters: The framework offers concrete design principles and auditing metrics to build scalable, stable, and robust adaptive machine learning systems across statistical and foundation model paradigms.

papers.title: From Score Learning to Discretized Sampling: An End-to-End Generalization Analysis of Diffusion Models

summary.tldr: A unified framework providing an end-to-end total variation distance estimate for score-based diffusion models, linking finite-sample training, ResNet parameterization, and discretized sampling to generative fidelity.
key_points: Analyzes the transition from discrete-time, finite-sample score learning to the ideal population-level continuous-time objective using ResNet-type architectures.
Derives an end-to-end total variation (TV) distance error bound for the generated terminal distribution without assuming an oracle score function.
Decomposes overall generative error into four components: forward process truncation error, reverse-time discretization error, score learning generalization error, and optimization gap.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers a theoretical foundation showing how sample size, time discretization grids, and optimization accuracy jointly dictate final diffusion model sample quality.

papers.title: Hierarchical Copula-Gumbel-Top-\texorpdfstring{$K$}{K} Routing: Two-Sided Dependence Control for Frozen Mixture-of-Experts at Fixed Per-Token Routing Laws

summary.tldr: Hierarchical Copula-Gumbel-Top-K enables tunable positive within-group and negative cross-group token dependence without altering a frozen MoE model's per-token routing laws or conditional expected expert traffic.
key_points: Uses an exchangeable Gaussian copula to positively correlate Gumbel perturbations for related tokens and a tunable antithetic construction for negative cross-group dependence.
Preserves per-token ordered Top-K samples, mixture weights, and inclusion probabilities identical in distribution to independent routing given pre-routing logits.
Establishes a trade-off where positive within-group coupling increases realized expert load variance, whereas cross-group opposition reduces it relative to flat coupling.
Allows routing dependence to be tuned using a small, score-function-trained controller over frozen features without modifying or backpropagating through the base model.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows practitioners to independently control expert-set coherence and load balance in frozen MoE models without distorting individual token routing distributions.

papers.title: LARA: Lightweight Adapters in the Residual Stream for Composable Adaptation and Alignment

summary.tldr: LARA introduces Lightweight Additive Residual Adaptation, a method that reads hidden states and injects low-rank corrections directly into a frozen model's residual stream rather than modifying weight matrices.
key_points: Operates strictly in the residual stream of a frozen base model, leaving all base weights untouched.
Matches LoRA performance at equal parameter counts on code fine-tuning and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) tasks.
Enables inference-time scaling via a parameter (γ) to smoothly interpolate between base and adapted behaviors.
Supports hosting and per-token automatic routing of multiple behaviors simultaneously, demonstrated by running seven adapters on a 1.5B model with 33 MB overhead.
summary.why_it_matters: LARA allows low-memory, single-model deployment of multiple task-specific behaviors and preference alignments that can be dynamically routed per token or adjusted at inference without modifying base weights.

papers.title: Self-Boosting Vision-Language Models with Noisy Student On-Policy Self-Distillation

summary.tldr: NOPD is a self-distillation approach that post-trains vision-language models without external models or ground-truth data by using token-level clean-input predictions as supervision for corrupted inputs.
key_points: Exploits prediction discrepancies between clean and corrupted inputs to create an internal self-supervision signal.
Uses the model's own predictions under clean inputs as token-level targets while training on corrupted inputs.
Improves Qwen2.5-VL-7B by 20 points on the Geometry3K validation set using 2.1K training samples.
Yields a 7.4 point gain on MathVista and demonstrates improvements across three VLM architectures on 12 benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: NOPD enables vision-language models to self-improve and generalize without relying on human annotations, external teacher models, or ground-truth answers.

papers.title: SearchArt: Training Long-Horizon Search Agent with Scalable Synthetic and Verified Task

summary.tldr: SearchArt is a framework that trains long-horizon search agents using scalable task synthesis via evidence graphs, unified verification pipelines, and a multi-stage SFT and RL post-training process.
key_points: Synthesizes complex QA pairs and search trajectories using web documents and automatically generated evidence graphs.
Implements a verification pipeline to jointly check QA consistency, search trajectory quality, and retrieved evidence relevance.
Uses a multi-stage post-training pipeline combining supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning-based policy optimization.
Achieves scores of 74.39 on BrowseComp-ZH, 70.06 on BrowseComp, and 52.55 on Deepresearch-bench using a Qwen3.5-27B model parameter size.
summary.why_it_matters: SearchArt demonstrates that a 27B parameter open-weight model trained on verified synthetic trajectories can match or exceed frontier closed-source agents on complex deep-search benchmarks.

papers.title: Joint Optimization for Greedy Longest-match Tokenization

summary.tldr: JOLT formulates vocabulary learning for greedy longest-match tokenization as an integer program, aligning vocabulary optimization directly with deployment-time WordPiece-style inference.
key_points: JOLT uses an integer program with greedy-consistency constraints to ensure optimal vocabulary selection matches greedy left-to-right longest-match decoding.

To scale, JOLT solves a linear programming relaxation and iteratively introduces higher-order segmentations for unresolved pretokens, yielding rounded solutions within 0.008–0.176% of the LP lower bound.
LP bounds reveal BPE is within 1–2% of optimal compression under greedy longest-match decoding, and JOLT closes 89.6–99.4% of that remaining gap.
Evaluations across four scopes and 32k/64k vocabulary sizes show JOLT generates up to 0.78% fewer tokens than BPE on held-out validation data.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables near-optimal vocabulary compression for WordPiece-style tokenizers with mathematical guarantees, reducing sequence lengths and downstream processing costs.

papers.title: Verbalized Particle Posterior: Bayesian Inference over Natural Language Hypotheses

summary.tldr: The Verbalized Particle Posterior (VPP) frames Verbalized Machine Learning as Bayesian inference, using Metropolis-Hastings or Sequential Monte Carlo to maintain a population of natural-language hypothesis particles.
key_points: Treats natural-language prompts as particles updated via VPP-MH or VPP-SMC, predicting through Bayesian model averaging without requiring access to LLM logits or gradients.
Unifies model structure and parameter selection within a single natural-language posterior space.

Outperforms single VML runs on regression, classification, and rule-discovery benchmarks, matching or exceeding oracle-best independent VML ensembles while eliminating catastrophic single-run failures.
Produces an interpretable posterior where individual particles can be inspected to evaluate plain-text hypotheses supported or rejected by data.
summary.why_it_matters: VPP brings principled uncertainty quantification and improved reliability to prompt-based learning while preserving human-readability of the underlying model hypotheses.

papers.title: Predict before you train: Scaling Laws for particle physics foundation models

summary.tldr: Researchers established joint model-and-data scaling laws for jet-based transformer foundation models, accurately predicting pretraining loss and downstream physics performance over two orders of magnitude in compute.
key_points: Fitting a joint model-and-data scaling law across three orders of magnitude of compute predicts the pretraining loss of 100x larger models to within one percent.
Lower pretraining loss systematically correlates with lower fine-tuning loss and higher background rejection on top tagging and quark/gluon benchmarks.
The resulting frontier transformer matches state-of-the-art physics-aware foundation models in accuracy, AUC, and quark/gluon rejection, trailing slightly only in high-purity top tagging.
The authors released five pretrained model sizes along with the complete training code and recipe.
summary.why_it_matters: Particle physics researchers can now translate compute budgets into expected downstream physics performance before allocating expensive training resources.

papers.title: Explaining BiomedCLIP with Weighted Banzhaf Interactions Supported by Tree-Gram Parsing

summary.tldr: ParseFIxLIP introduces Tree-Gram Parsing using spaCy dependency trees to group subword tokens into semantically coherent units for the Banzhaf interaction game in BiomedCLIP.
key_points: Combats subword fragmentation in vision-language models where clinical terms like 'saddle embolus' get split into meaningless subwords.
Utilizes a smart_depth grouping strategy based on spaCy token dependency trees to form semantically informed explanation players.
Mitigates combinatorial explosion in Banzhaf interaction games by reducing interaction possibilities and target dimensionality.
Validated on the ROCOv2 medical imagery dataset using BiomedCLIP to demonstrate semantic parsimony and cross-modal attribution stability.
summary.why_it_matters: It produces semantically coherent and clinically relevant cross-modal explanations for VLM predictions, aiding trustworthy deployment in medical AI settings.

papers.title: CAPT: A Multi-task Continuous Autoregressive Transformer enabling Cross-dataset and Cross-species Transfer for Calcium Population Dynamics

summary.tldr: CAPT is a continuous autoregressive population transformer that uses continuous patch tokenization to enable cross-dataset, cross-paradigm, and cross-species transfer for calcium imaging neural dynamics.
key_points: Uses a continuous patch tokenization strategy to model continuous calcium traces directly via end-to-end autoregressive pretraining.
Pretrained on a large-scale mouse dataset and evaluated on independent mouse, larval zebrafish, and C. elegans datasets using a frozen backbone with trainable adaptation modules.
Outperforms specialized and general-purpose baselines across neural population forecasting and behavior decoding downstream tasks.
Multimodal analyses with C. elegans NeuroPAL annotations demonstrate that CAPT embeddings capture anatomical cell-identity structure and build a shared functional space across datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates a viable pathway toward general-purpose neural foundation models that transfer functional representations across distinct species and experimental setups without fine-tuning the primary backbone.

papers.title: Structure over Depth: A Single-Block Spatio-Temporal Transformer for Multi-Entity Reasoning

summary.tldr: A single-block spatio-temporal transformer factorizes multi-entity interactions into explicit spatial, temporal, and cross-attention components, matching deeper architectures with only 1.76M parameters.
key_points: Decomposes multi-entity temporal dynamics into spatial interactions among entities, temporal interactions over time, and cross interactions coupling both domains.
Uses a single structured block featuring parallel spatial and temporal self-attention, followed by bidirectional cross-attention.
Combines the parallel and cross-attention outputs using a learnable gated fusion mechanism.
Evaluated on video-based group activity recognition, skeleton-based human interaction analysis, and wearable sensor-based activity recognition.
summary.why_it_matters: Explicitly structuring spatio-temporal interactions enables highly efficient multi-entity reasoning without relying on computationally expensive, deep transformer stacks.

papers.title: ADAGE: A Language-Agnostic Pipeline for Analogical Reasoning Evaluation

summary.tldr: ADAGE is a language-agnostic pipeline combining native-speaker curation with LLM generation to build abstract analogical reasoning benchmarks without relying on English translations.
key_points: Evaluates culturally-grounded reasoning by eliminating translation artifacts found in standard English-derived benchmarks.
Validated by creating translation-free benchmarks for Arabic, Amharic, and Japanese.
Tested across 14 open-weight models, revealing a accuracy drop of 12 to 52 percentage points on non-English benchmarks compared to English proverb reasoning.
summary.why_it_matters: It exposes severe performance drops in multilingual LLMs on native cultural reasoning tasks that traditional translated benchmarks mask.

papers.title: Stress-testing large language model agents in a robotic chemistry laboratory

summary.tldr: Researchers stress-tested LLM agents using a 45-workstation robotic chemistry laboratory across 4,608 trials to measure physical executability and evidence-driven replanning abilities.
key_points: Overall success was low: only 3.3% of total trials and 28.1% of the best system's trials yielded expert-assessed executable workflows under real constraints.
Long-horizon planning failed consistently, with only three executable workflows exceeding 30 operations out of a maximum of 44.
Experimental feedback across five rounds generated local adjustments but failed to induce high-level workflow replanning or analytical-method redesign.
summary.why_it_matters: The study exposes a severe gap between theoretical plan generation and physical-world execution, proving current LLM agents are unprepared for autonomous scientific research without better grounding.

papers.title: Guarantees on Dynamical System Distinguishability for LLM Token Generation

summary.tldr: A theoretical framework formalizes LLM token generation as stochastic linear dynamical systems, establishing lower bounds on non-dynamical classification errors and proving misclassification probability decays exponentially with sequence length.
key_points: Classification ignoring token dynamics faces an accuracy floor because the total variation distance between stationary marginal distributions of two dynamical systems (DSs) can be arbitrarily small despite substantial structural differences.

Misclassification probability in DS-based classification decays exponentially in sequence length $L$, driven by a dynamical discriminability factor $δ^2$ that measures spectral distance between systems.
Cross-embedding generalization is bounded via an approximate intertwining condition, where transferable discriminability depends on the smallest singular value of the intertwining map.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides mathematical guarantees explaining why tracking sequential token trajectories outperforms static marginals for distinguishing LLM outputs, alongside conditions for transferring models across different embedding spaces.

papers.title: WCM: World-Cognition Model for Generalizable Human-Robot Interaction

summary.tldr: The World-Cognition Model (WCM) introduces an embodied agent using the SLAK architecture and an asynchronous runtime to enable real-time, interactive human-robot collaboration and teaching.
key_points: Built on the SLAK (Sensing, Logic, Action, and Knowledge) architecture to decouple perception, reasoning, control, and memory.
Employs an asynchronous runtime that allows reasoning, dialogue, and robot execution to run concurrently.
Features a human-in-the-loop teaching mode where teaching episodes and task rollouts are converted into chain-of-thought (CoT) supervision for continuous learning.
Achieves a 73.8% average success rate across nine real-world interaction tasks, including held-out scenarios and long-horizon tasks learned via teaching.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides users with mechanisms to redirect, correct, and teach physical robots in real time, bridging the gap between fluent software language agents and physical task execution.

papers.title: When Can Depth Replace Precision? A Resource Theory of Quantized Neural Computation

summary.tldr: A resource theory uses relaxed controls to establish exact structural limits, convergence rates, and execution semantics governing when depth can replace precision in quantized neural systems.
key_points: Distance to the closed relaxed reachable set defines an absolute structural accuracy floor that increased depth cannot overcome for a declared operation library.
Pure schedules approach the relaxed reachable set at rate O(D^-1) under bounded-variation time dependence and O(D^-\vartheta + D^-1) under H\u00f6lder dependence of exponent \vartheta.
Full-state write-back introduces a D\rho_z penalty that can freeze updates, while increment error feedback bounds errors to a carry term and satisfies a common-lattice conservation law.
Matching accuracy for coherent depth-L first-order high-precision comparators requires depth scaling of D=\Theta(L).
Companion software provides verified primal and dual bounds for pre-training feasibility decisions, with the discrete core machine-checked in Lean 4.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes mathematically rigorous limits and execution conditions for trading numerical precision for architectural depth prior to training quantized networks.

papers.title: Hallucination Rates in Language Generation

summary.tldr: This paper formalizes language generation in the limit under infinite hallucination, proving that allowing errors at a limited rate strictly expands the set of learnable language collections and establishes a hierarchy based on hallucination rate and breadth.
key_points: Allowing infinite errors at a zero-measure rate makes language generation in the limit strictly more powerful than requiring finite error.
The theoretical framework reveals a strict hierarchy of uncountable language collections characterized by their hallucination rate and breadth (the generated fraction of the target language).
In repetition-free generation, comparing the sets of correct and incorrect strings generated similarly yields a strict hierarchy across every hallucination rate and breadth.
summary.why_it_matters: Formalizing hallucination rates provides a rigorous theoretical framework to analyze the fundamental tradeoff between error frequency and model capability in automated language generation.

papers.title: Logit-Coordinate Generative Models for Mixed Continuous-Categorical Tabular Data

summary.tldr: Logit-Coordinate Generative Models map categorical variables to smoothed natural parameters, enabling Flow Matching and Gaussian diffusion to handle mixed continuous-categorical tabular data, particularly under severe class imbalance.
key_points: Encodes categorical features as scaled-logit coordinates alongside transformed continuous features for unified Euclidean space processing in Flow Matching (FM) and diffusion models.
Introduces a mixed-distribution discrepancy that isolates categorical marginal error from conditional continuous Wasserstein error.
Provides theoretical stability bounds and imbalance-aware nonparametric error rates connecting drift/vector-field estimation errors to output sample quality.
Block-Conditional Logit FM and Logit Diffusion outperform or match standard one-hot encoding baselines across four real-data benchmarks and synthetic rare-cell imbalance tests.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework improves generative modeling accuracy for complex tabular datasets containing both continuous variables and heavily imbalanced categorical features.

security.title: On AI Safety and Security Technical Debt in Engineering AI-Enabled Systems

summary.tldr: This study introduces AITD-MAP, an integrated framework mapping a taxonomy of 31 AI technical debt types across 7 root-cause classes to 18 safety and security risks, backed by 34 actionable mitigation guidelines.
key_points: Systematic review of 60 primary studies categorizes 31 distinct AI Technical Debt (AITD) types into a root-cause taxonomy of 7 classes.
Maps identified AITDs to 18 trust-related concerns, specifically 6 safety hazards and 12 security vulnerabilities.
Synthesizes 34 lifecycle mitigation guidelines consisting of 8 safety-focused and 26 security-focused strategies.
Introduces the AITD-MAP framework based on AI TRiSM principles to connect debts, risk impacts, and mitigation techniques for software engineers.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides AI software engineers with a structured framework to make latent safety and security technical debts visible and actionable across complex, tightly coupled AI pipelines.

security.title: Accountable yet Anonymous AI Agents - Split-Knowledge Binding in National Agent-Identity Layer in China

summary.tldr: China is deploying a national agent-identity layer using split-knowledge binding to enable agent accountability while maintaining business-layer anonymity from commercial entities.
key_points: Split-knowledge binding uses a structural and procedural separation across two separate government agencies rather than cryptographic mechanisms to hold identity escrow.
Re-identification of an agent's verified legal principal requires legal due process to compel both holding agencies simultaneously, as neither agency can re-identify independently.
The paper introduces the ex-post attribution thesis, claiming that only attribution-based accountability holds legal force for AI agent actions with legal consequences.
The architecture defines an 'accountability surface' to map which specific agent actions generate identity-bearing traces.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates a national-scale framework for balancing user privacy with regulatory accountability for autonomous AI agents without relying on cryptographic primitives.

security.title: False Prophets: On the Security of World Models in Agentic Systems

summary.tldr: Researchers identified security vulnerabilities in text-based world models used by autonomous terminal agents, demonstrating that induced mispredictions can trigger unintended command execution, data extraction, and financial loss with up to a 95% success rate.
key_points: Identified vulnerabilities unique to text-based world models in terminal agents that enable malicious code execution, denial of service, wallet drainage, and sensitive data extraction.
Demonstrated that attackers can manipulate approximate world models to cause mispredictions in agentic pipelines with success rates up to 95%.
Introduced a new security benchmark dataset specifically designed for evaluating vulnerabilities in text-based world models.
Provided practical mitigation recommendations to harden agentic systems against world model exploitation.
summary.why_it_matters: Integrating unhardened world models into autonomous agents creates high-impact security risks, allowing attackers to manipulate an agent's predictive logic to execute arbitrary terminal commands or exfiltrate private data.

security.title: Hiding in Plain Sight: An Effective Physical Adversarial Patch Attack against Visual-Infrared Fused Face Detection

summary.tldr: VIPatch introduces a novel physical adversarial patch attack against visual-infrared fused face detection models using jointly optimized, natural-looking gradient-color masks and band-aid stickers.
key_points: Targets visual-infrared fused face detection models in both digital and physical domains.
Jointly optimizes a gradient-color mask and a band-aid sticker pattern across both visual and infrared modalities.
Uses digital patch optimization to guide the physical fabrication of inconspicuous adversarial patches.
Achieves attack success rates exceeding 90% in physical and digital evaluations while remaining unobtrusive to humans.
summary.why_it_matters: It reveals critical security vulnerabilities in multi-modal visual-infrared face detection systems using realistic physical artifacts that evade human detection.

security.title: GLST: Defending Confidence-Driven V2X Collaborative Perception Against Stealthy Multi-Attacker Feature Injection

summary.tldr: GLST defends V2X collaborative perception against stealthy feature injection by combining global feature, multi-scale local residual, and ego-semantic topology consistency signals.
key_points: Pretend Benign attacks exploit confidence-driven sparse V2X frameworks like Where2comm by injecting perturbations into uncertain yet perception-critical regions.
Single-signal trust defenses fail under multi-attacker scenarios because compromised nodes can establish a pseudo-consensus that manipulates trust estimation.

Global-Local Structural Trust (GLST) evaluates collaborators using three signals: global feature consistency, multi-scale local residual consistency, and structural consistency with ego-side semantic topology.
On the OPV2V dataset under a four-attacker Pretend Benign attack, GLST retains an AP@0.3 of 0.69, outperforming single-signal defenses while resisting PGD gradient-based attacks.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents malicious connected vehicles from degrading 3D object detection in V2X networks, ensuring robust autonomous driving perception even during coordinated multi-node attacks.
